summary: A small, plain system build: a T80 with CTC, PIO and daisy-chain interrupt modules wired pin by pin like a Z80 board, plus a scan-time character video pipeline. The video is a per-pixel H/V counter pipeline that fetches video RAM and then a char ROM/RAM row, and drives RGB straight from the three character-RAM bitplanes. It does not reproduce MAME's per-frame gfxdecode loop or its palette table. Nothing is clearly carried over from MAME's C++, but the board-specific logic is thin and mostly generic (range-compare decode, invented raster timing), so the hardware lean is mild.

findings.signal: scan-time pixel pipeline instead of frame batch
findings.note: Free-running cnt_h/cnt_v feed a staged pipeline: video RAM address from pos_y(7:3)&pos_x(8:3), then char address code(6:0)&pos_y(2:0), then a pixel picked by pos_x(2:0). MAME instead loops over all 0x800 offsets once per frame and calls gfx->opaque.

findings.signal: bitplanes wired directly to RGB, no palette
findings.note: The three character-RAM planes drive red/green/blue directly (Datac->R, Datab->G, Dataa->B), and ROM chars drive all three guns from one bit. MAME goes through a 10-entry palette with pens offset by 2. The core expresses this as wiring.

findings.signal: char RAM as three physical 1K plane RAMs
findings.note: ec00/f000/f400 are three separate dual-port 1K RAMs, all read in parallel by the video side at one address. That is how plane memories sit on a card. MAME's version is a gfx_layout with plane offsets and dirty-marking on writes (polyplay_characterram_w), which the core does not have.

findings.signal: CTC CLK/TRG inputs wired to a board clock
findings.note: All four CTC CLK/TRG pins are driven by a derived clock (CPU clock enable /4). MAME's machine config leaves the CTC trigger inputs unconnected. This is board wiring that MAME does not model.

findings.signal: Z80 peripherals as pin-level chips with partial I/O decode
findings.note: CTC and PIO chip selects are decoded from A7..A2 plus IORQ/M1 ("100000"/"100001"), with A0/A1 going to the chips' B/A and C/D select pins and M1/IORQ/RD to their ports. This is glue logic, not a handler-based port map.
These are general CTC/PIO/daisy-chain models with RETI detection, closer to a shared chip library than board logic. MAME uses the same CTC-then-PIO priority, which a correct core must share anyway.

findings.signal: memory map as address range compares
findings.note: RAM write enables and read-mux use >=/< range compares that match MAME's address_map ranges for both ZRE and ZRE-PP, selected by tno. This is a required shared memory map, not a gate-level decode.

findings.signal: CTC ZC/TO toggles a flip-flop for sound
findings.note: A rising ZC/TO edge sets a flag, and the level is toggled into a square wave. This matches MAME's flipflop toggle, but it is also the obvious hardware (a T flip-flop on ZC/TO), so it does not discriminate.
A divider from 50 MHz makes a 100 Hz low pulse into NMI. This matches MAME's periodic interrupt, and the mains zero-cross source on the board would give the same rate.

PIO port B bits 2:0 are either decoded to MiSTer LEDs, much like MAME's lamp[i] = (state == i), or passed raw to the user port for an external DS8205D decoder. The raw passthrough is hardware-oriented, but this is I/O plumbing.

H total 673 and V total 313, with sync windows at cnt_h<40 and lines 281-283, are fitted constants and not derived from board counter chains. They match neither MAME's 512x256 screen config nor any visible board-level timing chain.
